overview:
This check collects metrics from [cert-manager][1].

![Cert-Manager Overview Dashboard][2]

**Minimum Agent version:** 7.22.0

[1]: https://github.com/jetstack/cert-manager
[2]: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DataDog/integrations-core/master/cert_manager/images/overview_dashboard.png
setup:
Follow the instructions below to install and configure this check for an Agent running on a host. For containerized environments, see the [Autodiscovery Integration Templates][3] for guidance on applying these instructions.

### Installation

The cert_manager check is included in the [Datadog Agent][3] package.
No additional installation is needed on your server.

### Configuration

1. Edit the `cert_manager.d/conf.yaml` file in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your Agent's configuration directory to start collecting your cert_manager performance data. See the [sample cert_manager.d/conf.yaml][4] for all available configuration options.

2. [Restart the Agent][5].

### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][6] and look for `cert_manager` under the Checks section.

troubleshooting:
### Duplicate name tags

Each certificate name is exposed within the `name` label in the Prometheus payload and is converted to a tag by the Datadog Agent. If your hosts also use the `name` tag (for instance, automatically collected by the [AWS integration][9]), metrics coming from this integration will present both values. To avoid duplicate `name` tags, you can use the [`rename_labels`configuration parameter][10] to map the Prometheus label `name` to the Datadog tag `cert_name`. This ensures you have a single value within the tag `cert_name` to identify your certificates :
```yaml
init_config:
instances:
- openmetrics_endpoint: <OPENMETRICS_ENDPOINT>
  rename_labels:
    name: cert_name
```

Need further help? Contact [Datadog support][11].

[9]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/amazon_web_services/
[10]: https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/81b91a54328f174c5c1e92cb818640cba1ddfec3/cert_manager/datadog_checks/cert_manager/data/conf.yaml.example#L153-L155
[11]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/help/

metrics.name: cert_manager.certificate.expiration_timestamp
metrics.description: The date after which the certificate expires. Expressed as a Unix Epoch Time

metrics.name: cert_manager.certificate.ready_status
metrics.description: The ready status of the certificate

metrics.name: cert_manager.certificate.renewal_timestamp
metrics.description: The date at which the certificate will be renewed. Expressed as a Unix Epoch Time

metrics.name: cert_manager.clock_time
metrics.description: The clock time given in seconds (from 1970/01/01 UTC)

metrics.name: cert_manager.controller.sync_call.count
metrics.description: The number of sync() calls made by a controller

metrics.name: cert_manager.http_acme_client.request.count
metrics.description: The number of requests made by the ACME client

metrics.name: cert_manager.http_acme_client.request.duration.count
metrics.description: The count of the HTTP request latencies in seconds for the ACME client

metrics.name: cert_manager.http_acme_client.request.duration.quantile
metrics.description: The quantiles of the HTTP request latencies in seconds for the ACME client

metrics.name: cert_manager.http_acme_client.request.duration.sum
metrics.description: The sum of the HTTP request latencies in seconds for the ACME client

serviceChecks.name: cert-manager OpenMetrics health
serviceChecks.description: Returns `CRITICAL` if the agent fails to connect to the OpenMetrics endpoint, otherwise `OK`.
